intro: One register of everything the business owns and keeps: who has each asset, where it is, what state it is in, how it is looked after and what it is worth in the books, from the day it is put into service to the day it leaves.
start: Set up your asset categories and classes, with the useful life and depreciation each one follows.
Add the places where assets are kept, from site to room.
Register your assets, one at a time or by importing a file, and print their tags.
Assign each asset to the person or place that has it.
Set maintenance schedules for what needs regular upkeep, and make a depreciation run at the end of each month.

articles.summary: Turn goods you received or hold in stock into assets, one per unit, at what they cost, with the entry posted for you.

Each unit becomes an asset with its share of the cost, and the cost moves into fixed assets in the books.

tips: An asset that costs less than your capitalisation threshold is expensed: it is kept and tracked, but never depreciated.
An asset's page can trace it back to its goods receipt, order, supplier and invoice.

articles.title: Run depreciation for the month
articles.summary: Work out what each asset lost in value this month, have it reviewed, and post one entry to the ledger.

steps.rest: on Depreciation, choose the month and press Make the run.

steps.lead: Wait while it is worked out.
steps.rest: It becomes a draft with one line per asset: its value before, the amount and its value after.
Someone other than the person who made the run reviews it, where your settings ask.
One balanced entry is posted, dated the month's last day, and each asset's value goes down.

tips: Months are run in order: a month only after the one before is posted.
If assets changed after the run was made, it is refused. Press Cancel the run and make it again.
Your settings can make the run each month by itself.

articles.title: Revalue or impair an asset

articles.after: Depreciation from the next month is worked out from the new value.
